employer: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Thoracic Surgeon
locations: Cambridge Bio Medical Campus, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
This is a Substantive Consultant Surgeon post at Papworth Hospital. The post-holder will be expected to be proficient in adult general thoracic surgery as practiced in the UK.

The post-holder will work with the existing team of NHS Consultant Surgeons.

This job is currently based around fixed operating sessions and flexible cover for the other thoracic surgery sessions (currently 6 operating days Mon-Fri with ad-hoc Saturday lists).

Have responsibility for patients admitted under the care of the thoracic surgical service, and provide assessment, treatment and follow up for patients requiring thoracic surgery. Provide a cohesive service with the other Consultants and contribute to the smooth running of Thoracic Services.

Maximise thoracic surgery operating session use through developing and providing cover for both external and internal MDTs.

Contribute to the training of junior doctors in accordance with standards required by college, Postgraduate Dean and hospital. Demonstrate a commitment to continuing professional development and work with the team to build the academic activities of the thoracic surgery group.

Work with the team to support thoracic surgical / oncological related research, as part of an agreed research programme, and to contribute to audit activities.

The on-call Consultant Surgeon at Papworth Hospital also provides cover for thoracic trauma at Addenbrooke's Hospital and occasional, emergency cases from the rest of the Eastern Region.

The post holder will participate in an on-call consultant rota for thoracic surgery which is on a 1 in 4 basis. Currently there are separate on-call rotas for thoracic surgery, cardiac surgery and cardiothoracic transplant surgery, and the surgical group works effectively together.

Clinical support is provided by the resident surgical team, advanced nurse practitioners who are ward based and surgical care practitioners (SCP) on a firm and rota system.

Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the UK's leading heart and lung hospital, delivering care to more than 50,000 patients a year in its new state-of-the-art hospital in Cambridge. We perform the most heart and/or lung transplants in the UK and carried out the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979. It also offers emergency heart attack treatment, sleep centre care and is one of just five centres nationally for those in severe respiratory failure.

Based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus the largest centre of medical research and health science in Europe the Trust is at the heart of treatments of the future. Royal Papworth became the first hospital trust in the country to be rated outstanding in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission - a rating it still holds today. The Trust holds its values of compassion, excellence & collaboration at its core, and all colleagues joining the team are expected to uphold these in their day-to-day roles & interactions. Royal Papworth is proud of its diverse workforce and encourages people to embrace their individuality.

The Trust values difference and welcomes all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy & maternity, race, religion & belief, sex and sexual orientation. Providing they meet the minimum post criteria, applicants with disabilities will be offered an interview.

For a street view tour: https://royalpapworth.nhs.uk/virtual-tour

title: Salaried GP with a view to partnership
descriptionHtml:
We are a forward-thinking and dynamic GP practice, committed to providing high-quality care to our patients. We are looking for a dedicated and enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our team for 5/6 sessions per week. We offer a supportive and collaborative working environment, and we're excited to provide an opportunity to be considered for partnership in the future.

The surgery has comprehensive administrative support enabling our clinicians to focus on patient care during their 15 minute consultations. We are a Total Triage surgery using SystmOne and in addition use a variety of innovative online consultation tools like Accurx, SystmConnect.

The surgery is part of the NIHR East Midlands Research Delivery Network and a Training Practice with North Oxfordshire GP Trainee Scheme.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Patient Consultations: Manage both routine and urgent appointments via face-to-face and telephone consultations, ensuring safe, evidence-based, and individualised care.
  • Clinical Examinations & Care Plans: Perform comprehensive clinical assessments, addressing both physiological and psychological needs. Develop personalised care plans with timely referrals in line with practice, PCN, and local guidelines.
  • Independent Prescribing: Prescribe independently within your scope of practice, adhering to local or national prescribing guidelines, and promote health strategies that encourage patients to adopt healthier lifestyles.
  • Home Visits: Manage routine and emergency home visits as required.
  • Administrative Responsibilities: Handle routine administrative tasks such as responding to queries, managing repeat prescriptions, reviewing patient test results, and preparing referral letters or correspondence in a timely manner.
  • Clinical Management: Oversee patient care, initiate investigations, review results, and make appropriate referrals to secondary care or other providers, developing treatment plans that align with disease management protocols and NICE guidelines.
  • Collaboration: Work alongside other health and social care providers to ensure integrated care and maintain accurate, up-to-date patient records.
  • Team Support: Support both clinical and administrative staff in maintaining high standards and meeting practice targets.

Brackley Medical Centre is an innovative and supportive training practice which aims to provide high quality, safe and personalised patient care to over 16,000 patients. We are based in a purpose built health care facility which opened in 2020; the building is shared with both Northamptonshire Health Foundation Trust and Oxford University Hospital Trust who both operate a variety of secondary care services and satellite clinics; which provide our patients with unique local services for our semi-rural practice.

Focussed on high quality patient care and employee development we have a wide multi-disciplinary team; including experienced GPs, compassionate nurses and HCAs and Advanced Clinical Practitioners who respond to patient on the day demand. As part of Brackley & Towcester PCN we have First Contact Physios, Clinical Pharmacists, Mental Health workers, Social Prescribers and Health Coaches. Together, we collaborate to ensure the best possible health outcomes for our patients through a holistic and integrated approach to care.

We are looking to recruit an Salaried GP for 5/6 sessions per week to join our friendly team; salary will be dependent on experience. We will review applications as they come in to facilitate prompt recruitment.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Radiologist with Specialist Interest in Chest Imaging
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is looking for a Locum Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Chest Imaging to support Lung Cancer Screening in a busy and expanding department, predominantly based at he Princess Royal Hospital (PRH), with responsibilities across both hospitals' sites.

Due to a rapidly expanding workload most interests can be accommodated. One cancer MDT is an expectation; a second interest can likely be accommodated. Lung biopsy skills are expected. The posts will include sessions at the two main hospital sites within an overall flexible group job planning format, with an agreed overall sessional make up as described below.

Apart from lung biopsy work, there is currently no dedicated respiratory imaging component such as a formal MDT. There may, however, be scope to develop a non-cancer MDT in the future, as much of this discussion is presently carried out informally through individual meetings or email correspondence with the chest physicians. The ability to cover the screening MDT would be highly valuable, and there may also be future opportunities to take on the Responsible Radiologist role.

Applications are welcome from candidates who wish to be considered for a part-time or flexible working arrangement. Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

  • Share in the general imaging workload and collaborate with colleagues to support tumour-specific and other sub-specialty reporting, using PACS.
  • Contribute to the general work of the department would be expected from the successful applicant, including reporting of the general radiographic examinations carried out within the main sites, as well as in the various community hospital locations in Shropshire and the CDC.
  • Maintain a general Radiology practice while contributing to sub-specialty areas, as per departmental needs.
  • To work flexibly according to changes in work patterns and requirements. Requirement to participate in the non-resident on call and resident evening and weekend working. On call overnight is outsourced from 8.30pm to 8.30am and weekdays and weekends after 5.30pm to provide a more palatable and sustainable work pattern. On site attendance will occasionally be necessary during on call periods.
  • General radiological sessions will include in and outpatient cross section as well as plain films and body ultrasound. General skills must be maintained to support the acute hospitals' needs in evening and weekend working.
  • Addressing GP and clinician queries and vetting are core to the role.
  • To be involved in the organisation and administration of the Radiology Department and teaching of other clinical staff including participation in regular clinico-radiological meetings with other Consultants.
  • To be involved in the training of junior Radiology staff.

employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Radiology - Chest Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly, forward-thinking team of 30 Consultant Radiologists at the Royal United Hospital Bath;

Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Chest Radiology (10 PAs).

The post is full time but anyone wishing to work part time is also encouraged to apply. The post includes participation in the evening and weekend and on call rota.

If you want to balance these professional opportunities with quality of life then Bath has it all. Bath is a beautiful Georgian city in the South West of England, and is England's only city with UNESCO World Heritage Site status. There is a wealth of cultural and leisure opportunities, some of the best state and independent schools in the UK, whilst only 90 minutes from London and on the doorstep of the beautiful diverse South West countryside.

This is a replacement post following retirement for a substantive Consultant Thoracic Radiologist.

The RUH will work alongside the existing thoracic radiologists to help deliver the expanding lung cancer service including reporting chest radiographs and CT, performing lung biopsy, and preparing and presenting at the weekly lung cancer MDT meeting. The RUH has a tertiary satellite specialist pulmonary hypertension service, affiliated with The Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust. Circa 250 referrals per annum are received from around the South West and Wales. The appointee will be involved in reporting CT and MRI for patients with suspected pulmonary hypertension and participating in the weekly PH MDT. There will be an additional requirement to report for and participate in the ILD MDT

An ability to contribute to the cardiac CT +/- MRI service is desirable although not essential. With a specialist cardiac CT list on average at least once a day, the department performs approximately 1200-1400 CTCAs per annum, including CT coronary angiography, aortic valve calcium scoring and TAVI planning scans. The RUH utilises FFRct post-processing analysis as part of the NHSE MedTech mandate.

Working for your organisation

At the RUH we're proud to put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff wellbeing, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial wellbeing. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

title: Prescribing Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for somebody who shares our idea of what a PCN should be - supportive of its member Practices, effective and innovative. You'll be prepared to work hard to look after your patients and work with the lead clinical pharmacist and pharmacy team, wider multidisciplinary team colleagues and PCN leadership team to maintain a resilient and sustainable PCN.

We would like someone to join our team who has at least 1 year experience working as a Clinical Pharmacist in General Practice.

Hours of work per week = 27 to 37 hours

The employer is Network North PCN Ltd

For an informal chat / visit please contact Marie Wragg, PCN Manager marie.wragg2@nhs.net or David Russell, Lead Clinical Pharmacist david.russell8@nhs.net

To apply, please send your CV and covering letter to Marie.wragg2@nhs.net or apply via NHS jobs.

The post holder is a prescribing clinical pharmacist who acts within their professional boundaries, working alongside a team of pharmacists across the PCN which is made up of 5 Practices.

They will improve patients health outcomes and the efficiency of the primary care team by providing direct, accessible and timely medicines and expertise including face to face contact with patients.

The post holder will be an integral part of the PCN, as well as part of a wider general practice and multi-disciplinary team. This includes being a conduit of patient medicines information into and out of hospitals. They will work to optimise medication issues to improve patient care and safety, and augment clinical staff in the management of patients, with minimal support needed from the Lead Pharmacist.

As part of their employment, the post holder will ideally have completed the CPPE pathway and must be an Independent Prescriber, equipping the prescribing clinical pharmacist to be able to practice and prescribe safely and effectively in a primary care setting.

The supervision and mentorship network will be provided to support the prescribing clinical pharmacist.

Network North PCN is a well-established Primary Care Network in North Sheffield, with a stable patient population. We have a compassionate and supportive team. We are committed, friendly and flexible. Key info:

- 5 Practices within the PCN

- On site duty GPs, available for questions/queries/support

- System One and EMIS practices

- Approx. 45,000 patients

- Commitment to CPD

- Emphasis on teaching within Practices

- Forward thinking, innovative and keen to embrace new ways of working

- Multi-disciplinary team - including an Advanced Care Practitioner, Care Coordinators, Clinical Pharmacists, GPs, Mental Health Workers, Pharmacy Technician, Physician Associates, Physiotherapists and Social Prescribing Link Worker

title: GP Educator - Medical Student Education
descriptionHtml:
Put medical education at the heart of your working week

Are you a GP with a passion for teaching who would like education to be the main focus of your role?

This is an exciting opportunity to join WellBN in an education-led post, with the substantial majority of your working week dedicated to supervising, teaching and supporting medical students rather than routine clinical sessions.

The role is particularly suited to a GP with an interest or background in medical education who enjoys helping students develop their clinical reasoning, consultation skills and understanding of patient-centred care.

Join us

If you would like to make teaching and student development the main focus of your working week, while retaining a smaller clinical commitment, we would love to hear from you.

There is an option to convert to a substantive post. Job-share applications are welcome.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments during recruitment.

For an informal conversation or to express your interest, please contact Susan King at susan.king72@nhs.net.

You will oversee Year 4 and Year 6 medical students during their placements, helping them connect their learning with the realities of modern general practice. Through supervision, case discussion, feedback and teaching, you will support their development as confident, thoughtful and compassionate future doctors.

The post comprises seven sessions dedicated to educational supervision, alongside one or two clinical sessions per week. We welcome job-share applications from GPs interested in sharing the educational and clinical responsibilities.

During student placements, the emphasis will be on education: overseeing the students learning, reviewing clinical cases with them, discussing their assessments and management plans, and providing constructive feedback.

Between student placements, clinical cross-cover is expected to support the wider practice team.

An exciting new chapter for WellBN

WellBN is preparing to launch a new organisation in January 2027, alongside an upcoming rebrand and under new management.

Were developing a progressive, modern approach to general practice, with compassionate patient care, collaborative working and staff wellbeing at its heart. Joining at this stage offers the opportunity to contribute to the educational environment as the organisation develops.

WellBN serves approximately 25,500 patients across our Brunswick, Burwash and Benfield sites in Brighton, Hove and Portslade.

Our team includes a strong pharmacy service, paramedics and practice nurses. We use SystmOne and Accurx Triage and care for a diverse community, including neurodiverse patients and trans, non-binary and intersex patients, with training and support provided.

This setting offers students exposure to the breadth of modern primary care and the opportunity to learn how different professionals work together to support patients.

employer: South West London and St Georges Mental Health NHS Trust
title: Specialty Doctor - Ellis Ward
descriptionHtml:
Specialty Doctor - Ellis Ward

Full Time - 10PAs

The Trust is seeking an energetic and motivated specialty doctor, ideally with Section 12 Approval, to work on male only acute inpatient ward to support the consultant psychiatrist in providing high quality clinical care to our patients

This post is based at Tolworth Hospital, Red Lion Rd, Tolworth, Surbiton KT6 7QU. Ellis Ward forms part of the inpatient provision of the Trust's Acute and Urgent Care Service Line, which includes 8 acute adult wards and a PICU, based on 2 sites, Springfield Hospital in Tooting, and Tolworth Hospital in Surbiton.

There are 10 Programmed Activities. These clinical sessions will be on Ellis Ward, within the Inpatient Services of South West London & St George's Mental Health NHS Trust ("the Trust").

The appointed Specialty Doctor will be clinically supervised by the Ellis Ward Consultant Psychiatrist (Dr Jose Felix Mendez Jimenez).

The job plan will be reviewed regularly and may be modified reflecting changing needs within the service.

Ellis ward is a mixed 20 bedded ward. Over the last 12months, on average, there were 12 admissions/transfers in, and 10 discharges/transfers out per month.

South West London and St George's Mental Health Trust was formed in 1998. Springfield University Hospital in Tooting is the largest site from which the Trust operates and has provided mental health services since 1841. It provides a range of mental health, learning disability and substance misuse services.

The Trust was originally known as the Pathfinder NHS Trust in 1994 and provided services for Wandsworth and Merton. In subsequent years its strategy was to grow and to become the main statutory provider of mental health services for South West London. The Trust took on Putney and Roehampton services in 1998, Sutton Mental Health Services in 1999, and Kingston and Richmond services in 2001 as the former health authorities were disbanded and primary care trusts were established. The different histories of services in different boroughs are still reflected in service models, cultures and partnership arrangements but a recent move to Service Lines has enabled more homogeneity across the five London Boroughs the Trust now covers.

The Trust now provides mental health services to five London Boroughs: Wandsworth, Merton, Sutton, Kingston and Richmond.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Urological Surgeon with interest in Paediatric Urology
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is seeking to appoint a substantive Consultant Urological Surgeon with a specialist interest in Paediatric Urology. The post will be predominantly based at The Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, with responsibilities extending across both hospital sites.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive and collaborative multidisciplinary team delivering high-quality urology services to a wide and diverse catchment population. The post has been designed to strengthen and further develop urological care across Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin, and Mid-Wales.

The successful candidate will bring expertise in General Urology alongside a subspecialist interest in Paediatric Urology.

Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

  • Provide independent consultant level care for patients, working alongside the wider consultant body to ensure high-quality continuous management.
  • Manage patients with a full range of urological conditions, delivering both elective and emergency care autonomously. This will include providing out-patient and day case activity to support care of children and young people.
  • Contribute actively to clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement activities, and support the education and supervision of junior medical staff and other staffing groups that are involved in patient care.
  • Undertake administrative responsibilities required to support safe and effective clinical practice.
  • To develop enhanced clinical skills, especially in the assessment and management of acutely ill patients.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.
  • To follow patients throughout their clinical pathways.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Senior GP Administrator
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a highly organised, proactive, and experienced Senior Administrator to join our busy and friendly primary care team at Honeypot Medical Centre.

The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of administrative services across the practice. They will lead and support a team of administrators while delivering efficient, patient-focused services that contribute to high standards of care, regulatory compliance, and practice performance.

The role involves overseeing patient registration processes, clinical recall programmes, document management, workflow allocation, appointment administration, referral processing, prescription support, and the maintenance of accurate patient records using EMIS and Docman systems. The post holder will also support the achievement of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) targets and other contractual requirements through effective patient recall and engagement processes.

As a Senior Administrator, you will act as a point of escalation for administrative queries, contribute to service improvement initiatives, support staff development, and work collaboratively with clinicians, management, and external agencies to ensure safe, efficient, and high-quality patient care.

  • Provide day-to-day supervision and support to the administration team.
  • Oversee patient registration and registration workflow processes.
  • Manage document scanning, coding, and workflow allocation through EMIS and Docman.
  • Coordinate and monitor recall programmes including:
    • QOF recalls
    • Cytology recalls
    • Immunisation recalls
    • NHS Health Check recalls
    • Learning Disability recalls
    • Diabetes recalls
  • Support the management of appointment scheduling and patient communications.
  • Process referrals, prescriptions, and clinical administration tasks.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records in accordance with information governance requirements.
  • Liaise with external organisations regarding the archiving and retrieval of patient medical records.
  • Monitor administrative performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and patient experience.
  • Support practice managers and partners in achieving operational and service delivery objectives.
  • Assist with staff training, induction, and development of administrative procedures.
  • Promote a culture of quality improvement, teamwork, and patient-centred care.

    • With over 80 years of service to the local community, Honeypot Medical Centre is a well-established and forward-thinking GP practice committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. We combine the values of traditional family medicine with innovative approaches and modern technology to meet the evolving healthcare needs of our population.

    Our modern, purpose-built premises provide an excellent working environment, featuring nine spacious consulting rooms used by our multidisciplinary team, including GPs, pharmacists, nurses, healthcare assistants, and physiotherapists.

    We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible environment for both patients and staff. The practice is fully accessible, with ramps, a disabled parking bay, accessible toilets on both floors, and lift access throughout the building.

    Joining Honeypot Medical Centre means becoming part of a supportive, collaborative team dedicated to delivering outstanding care while fostering professional development and continuous improvement.

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for enthusiastic and highly motivated Consultants in Anaesthesia to join our team at Leicetser General Hospital within the University Hospitals of Leicester.

The Department of Anaesthesia at Leicester General Hospital provides comprehensive anaesthetic services to a wide range of specialties, including obstetrics, elective orthopaedics, elective gynaecology, urology, general surgery, day-case surgery, and the High Dependency Unit (HDU).

Leicester General Hospital is a tertiary referral centre for urology and delivers major urological and gynaecological robotic surgery. The Pain Management and Sleep Medicine services are also based at this site.

The recently opened East Midlands Planned Care Centre (EMPCC) is now fully operational, providing day-case and 23-hour care across a broad range of surgical specialties, including general surgery, urology, gynaecology, ENT, and ophthalmology. The hospital has a total of 18 operating theatres, including two located within the EMPCC.

There is continued support for non-clinical professional activities both inside and outside the trust.

UHL is fully committed to continuing medical education for consultants.

Maintenance of the highest clinical standards in the management of patients.

To share with colleagues responsibility for the day-to-day management of patients.

To promote new ways of working and co-ordinating care for patients in the community and to ensure that services are based on effective and integrated partnerships across the health community.

Take part in multidisciplinary case conferences.

Supervise and train junior medical staff

To be involved in appraising and assessing juniors.

Teaching, research and administration.

To proactively develop the service.

To actively participate in both departmental and Trust matters concerning Clinical Governance and audit.

Our new strategy, developed with the support and feedback of colleagues, patients, and partners, is our compass for the next seven years (2023-2030).

We have four primary goals:

  • high-quality care for all,
  • being a great place to work,
  • partnerships for impact, and
  • research and education excellence

And we will embed health equality in all we do - taking active steps to reduce the avoidable differences in healthcare that some people face, working in partnership with communities.

Our strategy is underpinned by new values and we will work to ensure they are an everyday reality for all:

title: Deputy Chief Medical Officer for Safety and Delivery
descriptionHtml:
There has never been a more exciting time to join Devon Partnership NHS Trust, an organisation committed to improving the mental health and wellbeing of people across Devon and beyond.

As one of the leading providers of mental health, learning disability and neurodiversity services in the Southwest, the Trust is focused on delivering high-quality, safe and recovery-focused care. The Deputy Chief Medical Officer for Safety and Delivery will provide senior medical leadership across our quality and patient safety agenda, helping to strengthen clinical governance, translate learning from incidents, mortality reviews and clinical audit into meaningful improvement, and ensure that safe, effective care is delivered consistently across our services.

Working collaboratively with the Chief Medical Officer, Clinical Executive, clinical and operational leaders and partners, this is an opportunity to combine strategic leadership with a strong focus on delivery. You will help provide assurance on quality and safety, champion learning and continuous improvement, and support services to turn evidence, insight and learning into practical changes that improve outcomes and experience. This is a pivotal role for an experienced medical leader who wants to shape safer, more effective services and make a meaningful difference for patients, carers and communities across Devon.

We are passionate about promoting good mental health & wellbeing. We strive to use the expertise & resources within our organisation, and through our partnerships, to deliver high quality services that are safe & focused on people's recovery.

We are committed to developing a culture of coproduction, involving patients, families & carers in everything we do

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a motivated and experienced GP to join our friendly, multidisciplinary primary care team across the Hammersmith & Fulham Health Centres, based at Charing Cross Hospital and Hammersmith Hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to become an integral part of a team committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and continuously improving the services we provide to our local community.

As a Salaried GP, youll have the opportunity to use and develop your clinical skills while working closely with a wide range of healthcare professionals. Youll provide the full range of General Medical Services and play an important role in shaping and maintaining excellent standards of care across our Centres.

Were seeking a committed, enthusiastic and experienced GP with a broad range of clinical experience and skills.

The role is offered for a minimum of 6 sessions per week, providing an excellent opportunity for a GP looking for a rewarding role within a well-established primary care environment.

Youll also need to be a trained Mental Health First Aid Champion or Freedom to Speak Up Champion, reflecting our commitment to creating a workplace where colleagues feel supported, valued and able to thrive.

  • Provide a full range of medical services as defined in the GMS contract, additional and enhanced services where appropriate.
  • Make professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare professionals within the organisation.
  • Assess the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems.
  • Screen patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness.
  • Develop care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice; disease management protocols, provide counselling and health education.
  • Maximise the effective use of current clinical computer systems. Record clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to an agreed standard.
  • Compile and issue computer generated acute and repeat prescriptions (avoiding handwritten prescriptions whenever possible).
  • To take part in areas including clinical auditing and data collection.
  • Contribute to QOF and Northwest London Standard requirements and recording & code data appropriately
  • Attend team meetings and other clinical meetings as necessary.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist and Honorary Research Fellow, South Cumbria
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist (General Adult) and Honorary Research Fellow

We are excited to launch the recruitment to this new post, jointly developed by Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust and the University of Cumbria. The post holder will spend 6 PAs per week working with the General Adult Home Based Treatment Team (HbTT), based in Kendal and 4 PAs working as an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Cumbria as part of the Mental Health Leaders Award. This would be based at the Lancaster Campus of the University of Cumbria.

The contract for the clinical role with LSCft would be permanent. The Honorary Research Fellow element would be fixed term until the end of February 2029, since that is dependent on funding.

As part of the clinical role, the postholder would be expected to contribute to the out of hours On Call rota, for which additional remuneration would be paid.

The clinical element of the role would be with the well-established Kendal HbTT and you would work as part of a multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to provide a service for those living in the Kendal area. The main duties would involve outpatient clinics for both new referrals and ongoing reviews. You would be expected to lead the MDT and provide supervision to the Resident Doctors working with the team.

The University of Cumbria Mental Health Leaders Award (MHLA) is a £2.5mn NIHR funded research grant, aimed at building capacity and capability around applied mental health and inequalities research at the University of Cumbria. You will be contributing to the aim of the MHLA, to increase our understanding of what the research priorities around mental health and inequalities in Cumbria are, and develop the infrastructure to deliver this research. This part of the post will be based with the MHLA operational team at University's Lancaster Campus. You will be expected to be on site 1 day per week.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.

It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. Remuneration will be as set out in the terms of the New Consultant Contract according to previous experience.

The role:

At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).

Excellent peer support group

Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultants

Opportunities to be a clinical supervisor

Relocation package available.

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us. We also have an extremely active Medical Education department and support our Consultants in becoming Clinical & Educational Supervisors and nurturing their interests in this area. There are also opportunities to have a role in Digital Leadership if this is a passion for any of our Consultants.

title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist or Consultant Paediatrician with a Special Interest in Neurodevelopmental Disorders

This newly developed post is part of a substantial investment in the services offered to children and young people with neurodevelopmental disorders by Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership Trust (CWPT). The post holder will provide consultant input and leadership in a community setting as part of an all-age neurodevelopmental service.

The post holder's main objective would be to provide medical input to the neurodevelopment team who provide assessment and treatment for children and young people of school age with autistic spectrum disorders and ADHD. This will include completing assessments, providing consultation to other professionals, overseeing multidisciplinary treatment plans and appropriately prescribing medication if required.

In particular, they would be expected to assess complex cases such as:- where there is a significant risk of self-harm, harm to others or risk of neglect- where there is diagnostic uncertainty or complexity- where the interaction of potential illness and personality factors needs to be evaluated.

The post holder would be expected to see around 12 new patients a month and 48 follow up reviews per month. It is expected that this substantial new investment will address historical waiting lists for neurodevelopmental assessment.

title: Rehabilitation Medicine Consultant
descriptionHtml:
This is a replacement post which provides an opportunity for a committed and flexible individual to join the current consultants in developing specialist rehabilitation services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire and to evolve and adapt along with the service. The post is for a full time Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine and applications for those wishing to work on a less than full time basis would also be welcome.

The Lotus Rehabilitation Centre relaunched in December 2021 after NHS England approved funding for a new modular 2-storey block to be built on the Queen Alexandra Hospital Site, Portsmouth. Located adjacent to the current Rehabilitation block (which houses therapy services and the hydrotherapy pool), the ground floor provides a modern, air-conditioned 26-bed rehabilitation environment for both the Rehabilitation Medicine and Stroke Rehabilitation services (13 beds each). The centre contains 2 rehab gyms, a meeting room, patient social space as well as private access to outdoor rehabilitation and garden space. There is a bridge link to the main hospital, with easy access to other medical specialty services and imaging services.

In addition to inpatient rehabilitation, the service also provides Rehabilitation Medicine outpatient clinics, including a specialist spasticity service. The clinics are based at St Marys health care campus, Portsea Island. The service works in partnership with Steepers to provide consultant sessions at the dedicated Murrison accredited regional prosthetic services based at Portsmouth Enablement Centre, St Marys health care campus, Portsea Island.

The appointee will work closely with the other 2 Consultants in Rehabilitation Medicine in providing comprehensive Rehabilitation Medicine services in Portsmouth serving the regional footprint as well as improving, strengthening and developing specialist services. The post offers opportunities to include elements of acute outreach, inpatient and outpatient Neurorehabilitation, paediatric to adult transition clinics and Prosthetic Rehabilitation services subject to interests and negotiation. Opportunities also exist to contribute to Rehabilitation ongoing and future service development and governance; Educational Supervision; and Departmental and Care Group leadership roles. The service is part of the Wessex Trauma Network and there are additional opportunities to be involved with this as well as opportunities for the appointee to develop a research portfolio if desired, or to collaborate academically with the University of Portsmouth and Kings College in delivering the newly established Medical Degree Programme.

Here at Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, we are proud to provide expert, compassionate care for our local population. We are ranked as the third in the country for research, embedding education and training across the organisation. Our main hub is the Queen Alexandra Hospital, which is one of the largest hospitals on the south coast employing over 8,700 staff.

Our patients come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds because it makes our hospital stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for getting it right for patients, colleagues, and our community, you will find a home at Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust.

You will also be part of a Trust wide Consultant network where there are opportunities to liaise with colleagues in other posts throughout the Trust and develop peer networks.

  • To provide medical psychiatric assessment and intervention, including pharmacology and mental health act assessments to CAMHS in Coastal West Sussex ( Chichester and Worthing Bases ) ensuring best quality and most effective psychiatric care, working within a multi-disciplinary team.

You will have the opportunity to make a real difference to improve the lives of children and adolescents, working with colleagues in the team to provide a full range of outpatient and inpatient services and helping to manage transition between these and other services through outreach services.

You will be joining a Trust rated 'Good' by the CQC and 'Outstanding' for caring, with a strong commitment to innovation, research, and continuous improvement.

At Sussex Partnership we are committed to providing opportunities for flexible working. If you would like to work differently or different hours to as advertised, please get in touch to discuss this in more detail.

employer: Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in T&O (Special interest in Hand & Wrist Surgery)
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Substantive Trauma and Orthopaedic Consultant with a special interest in Hand and Wrist Surgery at Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust.

The successful applicant will join the Trauma and Orthopaedic Department which comprises of 12 substantive consultants and a multi-disciplinary team including 4 Specialty Doctors, 4 Fellows, 2 Specialty trainees, 7 trainees on first on call rota.

We are looking for a dynamic colleague to join our department and complement the existing clinical expertise. You will be part of a friendly, forward thinking team dedicated to providing high quality care for our patients.

The post holder will work as part of the orthopaedic team to provide a comprehensive service and continuing clinical responsibility for patients under their care. They will manage personal workload in such a way as to ensure that service contract levels are achieved and that work in excess of established contract is undertaken in accordance with the policy of the Trust.

Prospective candidates are encouraged to contact the department to discuss career aspirations or obtain further information about the post. Applications will be welcomed from both newly accredited trainees and established consultants.

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Bolton CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Bolton Community mental health teams (CMHTs) provide multi-disciplinary assessment, treatment, and care of individuals with severe and enduring mental health problems.

They service is available to residents of Bolton, aged 16 to 70 years, with a diagnosed functional mental health problem. This typically includes service users with:

  • Schizophrenia,
  • Severe Affective Disorder,
  • Complex Personality Disorder
  • Autism Spectrum Conditions
  • ADHD

Bolton operates a sectorised service. The sectors are defined by GP practice populations within the boundaries of the borough.

The South Sector post covers a population served by GP practices based at Stone hill, Level Chamber 1, Pikes lane, Orient House, Deane Clinic, Wyresdale, St Helen's Road, Peter House and Stable Fold Surgery. The sectors are reviewed in line with the changing profile of population and reflects the deprivation, referral patterns and throughput to ensure equitability among the four General Adult Community Consultants.

A full list of GPs and referral patterns are available.

The under 16 population is 60,000 and the over 65 population 40,000. The nominal catchment population therefore for each of the six General Adult Psychiatrists is just under 30,000.

The post holder will be based at the Barnett House, Community Mental Health Team on Weston Street, Bolton, where the other General Adult Community Psychiatrists are also based. He or she will be given an unshared office with a PC and fulltime secretarial support and is also to be supported by a full-time Core Trainee.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over 7000 members of staff, who deliver services from more than 122 locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford, Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Streatfield Health Centre is looking to recruit Salaried GP for three to four sessions per week.

We are a friendly, forward-thinking and enthusiastic practice caring for approximately 7800 patients.The ideal candidate will be at least three years post-qualification and will share our commitment to delivering high-quality, person-centred care within a supportive and progressive practice environment.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality, patient-centred primary care as part of our supportive team.

The role will include managing a varied clinical caseload through face-to-face and telephone consultations, assessing and managing both acute and long-term conditions, prescribing, making referrals and supporting continuity of care.

The Salaried GP will work closely with our GP Partners and wider clinical team and will contribute to clinical governance, practice meetings, quality improvement and the ongoing development of services within the practice.

Streatfield Health Centre is an established practice in Harrow. Wepride ourselves on having a friendly, supportive and collaborative working environment, where all members of the team are valued and encouraged to contribute to the development of the practice.

Were proud of the personal care we provide and the relationships we build with our patients and families. We know general practice can be busy and challenging, but we believe it should also be supportive, collaborative and rewarding.

Our team comprises of 2 GP Partners, 7 salaried GP'S, 1 registrar, 2 Pharmacists, 1 Practice Nurse, 2 HCA'S,1 registra and a supportive reception/administration team. Streatfield Health Centre is a training practice.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Upper GI Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a Consultant UGI Surgeon, with special interest in Upper Cancer surgery.

Based at the Royal Derby Hospital the UGI department provides a full range of out-patient diagnostic services and inpatient elective operating services for benign, bariatric and malignant disease as well as outpatient clinics and day case sessions. The department provides a full service to patients with Upper GI cancers across Derby-Burton and Bariatric services for the East Midlands, serving Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire.

There are currently 10 UGI consultants within the unit, supported by a team of resident doctors, clinical fellows and clinical nurse specialists.

The department has access to a 9 theatre inpatient suite and a 3 theatre Day Case facility. The inpatient theatre suite boasts two fully integrated laparoscopic theatres and the Trust offers Da Vinci Robotic cancer surgery in urology, colorectal, head and neck and UGI/HPB.

This post will be based across Royal Derby Hospital and with clinical activity also delivered at community sites across Derbyshire. The post holder will have a minimum 10 PA job plan including outpatient clinics, endoscopy, day case and inpatient operating as well as time for patient administration, ward rounds and supporting professional activities.

The post holder will provide emergency cover for general surgery (adults and paediatrics) as part of a 1 in 9 consultant day time rota and 1:18 nights and weekends rota.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

  • Development opportunities, both professional and leadership development
  • On-going support from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.
  • Staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts:

  • We see on average 4810 OP appointments a day.
  • We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.
  • An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.
  • Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.
  • Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.
  • We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.
  • We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.
  • UHDB is a research active University Hospital with a large and varied portfolio of clinical trials and research opportunities for all staff.

title: GP Womens Health - Menopause Care
descriptionHtml:
An exciting to join the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub as part of our innovative and Community Gynaecology Service.

We are ideally looking for GP's who have Advanced BMS/CoSRH Certificate in Menopause Care.

We are looking for enthusiastic and experienced General Practitioners with significant experience and passion for Women's Health who wish to develop advanced knowledge and practical skills within a supportive, multidisciplinary team.

Working alongside experienced GPwERs, Community Gynaecologists, and collaborative partnership, you will deliver high-quality, evidence-based care closer to home whilst helping transform women's healthcare across Berkshire West.

We have multiple roles available, ideally we are looking for Salaried GP's however we will consider locums.

An exciting opportunity to provide specialist assessment and management of women referred into the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within agreed clinical pathways whilst further developing your specialist skills, through a structured and supportive environment for professional growth.

Responsibilities include:

  • A mix of triage, virtual and face to face consultations
  • Assessment, diagnosis and management of a wide range of benign gynaecological conditions within the Community Gynaecology Service.
  • Independent management of patients within agreed competency levels.
  • Performing community-based gynaecological procedures appropriate to training and competence such as
  • Removal of lost IUS
  • Difficult insertion of IUS
  • Cervical polypectomy
  • Assess and manage incontinence and prolapse symptoms including vaginal pessary
  • Cervical cautery
  • Participation in MDT and other clinical meetings where appropriate.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit, teaching and service improvement initiatives and ensure service is complaint with CQC legislation.

The Primary Care Alliance is a primary care provider collaborative. We have 36 general practice members. The Alliance became a Community Interest Company in 2026.

Our mission

  • Our mission is to support and sustain the practice ownership model. We seek to do this through:
  • Acting as a united face of primary care across Berkshire West.
  • Supporting the collaboration of members whilst preserving local identity.
  • Giving members access to skills and capabilities they could not access by working alone.
  • Contracting for services that need to be provided at scale.

We are not:

  • Commissioners of health care services. We bid for services we think would best be provided through our primary care partners.
  • Legal or contractual representatives of general practices, these are the respective roles of the Local Medical Committee and the Integrated Care Board.
  • Competitors with practices and PCNs. If a component of primary healthcare is to be commissioned and is most appropriately delivered at practice or neighbourhood level then we are quite clear that the GP practice is sovereign, and in its turn, the PCN.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Locum Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a consultant Haematologist on a fixed term on a 12 months contract and will be based at University Hospital Lewisham (UHL).

The successful applicant will have the opportunity to help develop a high-quality service in this busy district general hospital, delivering comprehensive Haemoglobinopathy, Haemato-Oncology, General Haematology & Laboratory Haematology services.

The trust is in the process of operationalising a number of exciting service transformations, such as an Emergency Department Bypass Unit to improve the outcomes and experiences of our patients with sickle cell. The department is also exploring opportunities for the expansion of our treatment capacity for malignant and non-malignant haematology and is in the process of developing a strategy to adopt innovative ways of working. The postholder will have the opportunity to contribute to the clinical leadership of these exciting developments.

This role will be delivered as whole-time equivalent amounting to 10 programmed activities per week, subject to job plan review. Any applicant who is unable for personal reasons, to work full-time will be eligible to be considered for the post. If such a person is appointed, modification of the job content will be discussed on a personal basis with the Trust in consultation with consultant colleagues.

The appointee will be based at UHL to provide a General Haematology service as well as Haem- Malignancy service. Interest in Haemoglobinopathy will be welcomed

The general Haematology workload includes providing full haematological support to all patients treated at Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust, GPs and the local Mental Health Trust (Oxleas). The population served is approximately 800,000. Traditionally the Haematologists have had good working links with the GPs and have provided a direct consultative service for interpretation of haematological tests and clinical problems. Anticoagulation services are partially moving into the community.

The post holder is expected to take an equal share in the delivery inpatient haematology services including Level 2B, laboratory haematology workload including blood film, bone marrow and Transfusion Management.

The post holder may be required to undertake other duties appropriate for a Consultant Haematologist not otherwise specified.

title: Consultant Physician Care of the Elderly
descriptionHtml:
The Health Board wishes to appoint an additional Consultant Physician / Geriatrician to join the existing Care of the Elderly team in the West division of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB), North West Wales. This post is based in the district general hospital, Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor, and we would consider part-time working for the correct candidate.

The successful candidate will have a sub-specialty interest and we are open to considering a range of sub-specialty areas for the right candidate. This reflects our ambitions to develop a dedicated frailty unit within the acute hospital, alongside expanding community-based initiatives aimed at reducing avoidable hospital admissions. In view of the continued expansion of the North Wales Medical School, opportunities to undertake teaching and educational supervision commitments could be considered.

The successful applicant will be expected to:

  • Develop and support a recognised sub-specialty interest, such as acute frailty, community geriatrics or orthogeriatrics.
  • Provide supervision, teaching and support to junior medical staff and other healthcare professionals.
  • Contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, including students from Bangor, Cardiff and Swansea Universities.
  • Participate in clinical governance, quality improvement, audit, appraisal, revalidation and continuing professional development activities.
  • Contribute to service development and transformation projects across acute and community geriatric services.
  • Participate in research, education and innovation opportunities where appropriate

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services for the population of North Wales, across 3 acute hospitals and a network of communityhospitals, healthcentres, clinics, and mental health units. It alsoco-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

The Health Board is an integrated health system that strives for excellent, compassionate care delivered in partnership with the public sector and other statutory and third sector organisations.

title: Part-time Dispenser

We are seeking a Part-time Dispenser to join our dispensing team to provide quick, efficient and accurate dispensing of medication to patients.

title: Consultant in Palliative Care
descriptionHtml:
This is a replacement, permanent 8PA post which presents an exciting opportunity to contribute to a high quality, patient centered service in a supportive multidisciplinary team.

The post will cover both acute hospital inpatient work and work within community settings, ensuring patients can be seen and supported where ever they are.

The role involves delivering expert clinical care, providing specialist advice to healthcare professionals, participating in the on-call rota, and supporting the development of innovative services that enable patients to receive care closer to home.

The successful candidate will join a team of consultants in Palliative medicine supported by nurse specialists in both acute and community settings. There are opportunities to develop sub specialty interest where this contributes to and complements the department and Trusts' service needs. There are undergraduate & postgraduate education and research opportunities available.

To share with colleagues' responsibility for the day-to-day running of the Palliative Medicine department.

To provide direct and indirect specialist Palliative Medicine advice and support to hospital inpatients in West Suffolk Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

To provide direct and indirect specialist Palliative Medicine advice and support to patients in the community, in conjunction with colleagues at St Nicholas Hospice Care

To provide Palliative Medicine consultant input within the community through joint working with other specialties and other providers

To develop and deliver palliative care education to health care professionals at all levels

To participate in the consultant telephone 2nd on call rota across Suffolk and Great Yarmouth & Waveney

To contribute to the planning and further development of palliative care services in the area and across the ICB

Please see Job Description for full vacancy details

#BeKnown at West Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust. By us. By our patients. By our community

We are a busy, friendly, rural NHS Trust providing high-quality care and compassion to more than a quarter of a million people across west Suffolk. We care for, treat and support people in hospital, at home and in various community settings.

The West Suffolk Hospital in Bury St Edmunds provides acute and secondary care services (emergency department, maternity and neonatal services, day surgery unit, eye treatment centre, Macmillan unit and children's ward). It has 500+ beds and is a partner teaching hospital of the University of Cambridge.

Adult and paediatric community services, provided in collaboration with West Suffolk Alliance partners, include a range of nursing, therapy, specialist, and ongoing temporary care and rehabilitation, some at our Newmarket Community Hospital.

We do our utmost to achieve outstanding clinical outcomes for patients and our values of fairness, inclusivity, respect, safety and team work guide how we work and behave as a team.

With nearly 5,000 staff, from all over the world, we strive to make our organisation a great place to work. Whatever your role or ambition, we want to help you be the best you can be.

We promote a diverse and inclusive community where everyone's voice counts and you can #BeKnown for whoever you are.

Join us. What will you #BeKnown for?

title: High Intensity CBT Therapist - Part Time
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a High Intensity CBT Therapist in Scunthorpe on a part time basis.

As a High Intensity Therapist (CBT), you'll play a key role in supporting people experiencing common mental health difficulties alongside drug and alcohol use. Using evidence-based Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), you'll help people develop the skills and confidence to improve their mental wellbeing and achieve meaningful recovery.As a High Intensity CBT Therapist, you will:

Deliver evidence-based High Intensity CBT interventions to adults accessing our drug and alcohol services in Scunthorpe.
Undertake comprehensive assessments, develop formulations and create collaborative treatment plans tailored to individual needs.
Manage your own caseload, ensuring safe, effective and timely delivery of therapy.
Assess and manage clinical risk within your scope of practice, working closely with the wider multidisciplinary team.
Work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners to ensure seamless care and appropriate referrals.
Maintain accurate and confidential clinical records in line with professional, organisational and information governance standards.
Participate in regular clinical supervision, continuing professional development and service evaluation activities.
Support service development through clinical audits, outcome monitoring and sharing best practice.
Promote equality, diversity and inclusion while delivering trauma-informed, recovery-focused care.
Safeguard children and adults by following WithYou policies and procedures at all times.
Support our Mental Health and Wellbeing Practitioner with regular case management and clinical supervision.
As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. WithYou is all aboutWithYou provides free and confidential support, without judgement, to more than 100,000 people every year experiencing challenges with drugs, alcohol and mental health across England and Scotland.

employer: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Are you a GP looking for an exciting and supportive role within a forward-thinking multidisciplinary team?

Surbiton and Chessington PCNs are seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated GP to join our team under the NHS Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS). The role is for 6 sessions a week, ideally starting in early 2027.

employer: Milton Keynes University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in  Breast Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Milton Keynes University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is recruiting a Breast Consultant in Imaging. The postholder will deliver high-quality, patient-centred care and support the Trust's ambition to improve the health and wellbeing of our community.

This is a full-time, substantive post (10 PAs) supporting the diagnostic breast imaging service, collaborating with other consultant breast radiologists and the specialist mammography team.

Golden Hello and Relocation SupportThis post attracts a Golden Hello recruitment incentive of up to £20,000, comprising £10,000 on joining, followed by £5,000 on the first anniversary and £5,000 on the second anniversary of employment.

In addition, relocation expenses of up to £8,000 are available, subject to eligibility and the Trust's Relocation Expenses Policy.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and skilled Consultant Breast Radiologist to join our supportive and forward-looking Imaging Department. This is a full-time, substantive replacement post (10 PAs) supporting the diagnostic breast imaging service, working closely with our team of consultant breast radiologists and specialist mammography practitioners.

This is a replacement post.

We welcome applicants who have broad radiology experience consistent with a fully trained Consultant Radiologist, together with specialist expertise in breast imaging and experience of the National Breast Screening Programme.

This post will encompass all areas of imaging allied to the screening and symptomatic breast services, including specialist breast ultrasound, image guided intervention utilising the modalities of ultrasound, stereotactic guidance and digital breast tomography with special reference to stereotactic guided and ultrasound guided vacuum biopsy., the reporting of breast MRI, CT and plain radiography.

This post encompasses the full range of imaging associated with both the screening and symptomatic breast services. The successful applicant will undertake:

Breast Imaging and Intervention

o Specialist breast ultrasound

o Image-guided interventions using:

o Ultrasound guidance

o Stereotactic guidance

o Digital breast tomosynthesis guidance

o Stereotactic-guided and ultrasound-guided vacuum biopsy

You will also participate in the National Breast Screening Programme and contribute to the delivery of high-quality, patient-centred diagnostic services.

There will be opportunities to pursue and develop areas of special interest in line with departmental priorities and the Trust's strategic direction. We welcome applicants who bring initiative, innovation, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

The main base for this post will be Milton Keynes University Hospital but there may be a requirement to work at any other location where the Trust provides services such as community diagnostic centres.

Milton Keynes University Hospital, in proud partnership with the University of Buckingham, is a University Teaching Hospital committed to advancing patient care through cutting-edge research and education. With a "Good" rating from the CQC and significant investment underway, this is an exciting time to join our team and grow your career.

As a medium-sized general hospital, we provide a full range of general medical and surgical services, including a busy Emergency Department, Maternity, and Paediatrics. As the population of our city and surrounding areas continues to grow rapidly, we are expanding and enhancing our facilities to meet rising demand and improve access to care for all our communities.

We are also proud to offer a growing portfolio of specialist services. In January 2025 we opened our state-of-the-art Radiotherapy Centre, bringing advanced cancer treatment closer to home. employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Acute Physicians
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is looking for an enthusiastic individual with a passion to support the transformation programme of the trust moving into a single site emergency hospital who will be predominantly based at The Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, with responsibilities across both hospitals' sites.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality clinical care to acutely ill patients, working closely with multidisciplinary teams. The role involves leading the acute medical unit, offering expert guidance and supporting junior staff. You will contribute to service development and quality improvement initiatives. A commitment to teaching and ongoing professional development is essential. We are looking for individuals motivated enough to take on a leadership role in the department as a part of this job and share a CD role based at Royal Shrewsbury Hospital. This will be renumerated separately.

Candidates with Acute Internal Medicine training and/or GIM training wishing to do hybrid posts are encouraged to apply. We are also keen to support colleague's professional clinical areas of interest (e.g., Endocrinology or Respiratory to name a few) and are open to negotiations on your individual job plan.

Managing Acute take

  • Supervising the medical admissions ensuring timely junior team assessment and Consultant post take review of all new patients referred to acute medicine throughout the acute medical floor.
  • Leading and supporting the medical handover every morning including focusing on learning opportunities.
  • Driving the acute medical take and making sure patients are seen and dealt with efficiently and timely manner.
  • Ensuring national and hospital target of care and assessment of patients are complied with in a timely manner.
  • Provide advice and when appropriate review of patients when requested by the medical and nursing staff on the acute medical floor.
  • Engaging in timely discussions with subspecialties such as ITU/Cardiology/Renal (to name a few) in the care management of unwell acute medical admissions.

Same Day Emergency care (SDEC)

  • Prompt assessment of patients seen in this area including early senior reviews to initiate investigations required for rapid turnaround of these patients.
  • Facilitating 'PULL' and 'PUSH' of patients from the emergency department based on SDEC criteria.
  • Support the work of medical team and nurses in this clinical space.
  • Referral to the appropriate discharge support services where needed e.g. OPAT and Virtual ward.
  • Liaise with other specialties as required.
  • Good communication with Primary Care Colleagues to ensure smooth transition of care of patients once discharge.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Encompassing some of the most picturesque parts of England and Wales, the Trust's catchment stretches from the Cambrian Mountains in the west, to Newport and the fringes of the Black Country in the east. The main towns include: Bridgnorth, Ludlow, Market Drayton, Oswestry, Shrewsbury and Whitchurch (in Shropshire); Newport, Telford and Wellington (in Telford & Wrekin); and Newtown and Welshpool (in Powys) - all beautiful and unique.
