title: GP with Entended Role
descriptionHtml:
ProcareHaslemere Community Hospital

We are looking for experienced and enthusiastic GPs to join the Haslemere Proactive Care Hub, working as part of a multidisciplinary team supporting people living with frailty, multiple long-term conditions and complex care needs.

The Hub brings together primary care, community services and specialist expertise to provide more proactive, coordinated care closer to home.

Our aim is simple: to identify people who would benefit from additional support earlier, bring the right professionals around them and help prevent deterioration and avoidable hospital admission.

GP with Extended Role Proactive Long Term Conditions Hub4-6 sessions per week

We are also looking for GPs who have a particular interest in frailty, complex multimorbidity, long-term conditions and proactive community care.

This is predominantly a clinical role, working directly with patients and alongside the wider Hub multidisciplinary team.

You will undertake comprehensive assessment of people with frailty and complex needs, including Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA); provide GP clinical review and sense-checking of specialist recommendations; support medication optimisation; develop personalised care and anticipatory care plans; and work alongside specialist clinicians, pharmacists, therapists, community nursing, social care, mental health and other members of the MDT.

A particularly important part of the role will be bringing the generalist GP perspective to complex care looking beyond individual conditions and ensuring that recommendations are practical, coordinated and appropriate for the person as a whole.

You do not need to be a specialist geriatrician. We are looking for experienced GPs with an interest in developing this area of practice and enthusiasm for working differently across traditional organisational boundaries

Why join us?

This is an opportunity to be part of a developing model of care that brings primary care and community services together around some of our most complex patients.

You will have the opportunity to work closely with experienced clinicians from across primary, community and specialist care, influence how the Hub develops and help demonstrate what genuinely integrated, proactive care can achieve for patients.

based primarily at Haslemere Community Hospital.

For an informal conversation about either opportunity, please contact Jane Fagan, Chief Operating Officer.

To apply: Please submit a CV outlining your experience, and what you feel you could bring to the Haslemere Proactive Care Hub to procare.people@nhs.net

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a friendly, enthusiastic GP to join our welcoming team at Newport Surgery. Serving around 10,000 patients in a semi-rural community, we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality, compassionate care while maintaining the personal touch that general practice is all about.

As part of our supportive clinical team, you'll work alongside two GP Partners, five Salaried GPs, an ACP, Practice Nurses and a wide range of PCN-funded ARRS colleagues. We are a high-achieving QOF practice with a strong reputation for teamwork, continuity of care and excellent patient service.

Newport Surgery is a training practice with a genuinely close-knit and stable team. We value our staff, support professional development and are proud of our excellent retention of clinical colleagues. Whether you're looking to develop special interests, get involved in teaching, or simply enjoy working in a collaborative and supportive environment, you'll find a warm welcome at Newport Surgery.

If you're looking for a practice where your contribution is valued, your colleagues are supportive, and you can make a real difference to your local community, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Provide high-quality, patient-centred care through a mix of face-to-face, telephone and online consultations.
  • Assess, diagnose and manage a wide range of acute and chronic medical conditions.
  • Undertake home visits where appropriate.
  • Prescribe safely and effectively in line with national and local guidance.
  • Manage clinical correspondence, test results and other patient-related administration.
  • Work collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team, including Practice Nurses, the ACP and PCN-employed ARRS staff.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Burns Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Locum Consultant Plastic Surgeon with a Special interest in Burns, at the University Hospital Birmingham NHS Trust.

The post holder will work as one of a team of Consultant Burns and Plastic Surgeons, covering the Regional Burns Service in the Midlands. The adult burns centre is based at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, University Hospital Birmingham NHS Trust. Paediatric burns management takes place at the Birmingham Children's Hospital. In addition, the post holder will have the opportunity to do an additional plastic surgery subspecialities depending on experience and interests. The postholder will become an integral part of the Burns MDT Team . They will join a well-established and active team of burn surgeons who work across both hospital sites to provide care in both the Paediatric and Adult Burn Centres in Birmingham, as part of the Midlands Burn Operational Delivery Network.

The Job Plan will comprise of 10 programmed activities, including burns on-call across the QE hospital and Birmingham Children's Hospital. The job plan will be subject to the needs of the service and experience of the successful candidate. The final time table will be constructed following discussion with the successful candidate and will result in an agreed job plan. employer: Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Locum Consultant Psychiatrist - Forensic Services
descriptionHtml:
Leeds and York Forensic Services provide Low Secure Inpatient Services based at two sites within Leeds & York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (Clifton House, York and Newsam Centre, Leeds). The Forensic Service provides a high quality assessment, treatment and recovery service for people who represent a risk to others due to their mental disorder and are in need of either inpatient management, or support from a specialized community team. There are male acute and rehabilitation wards on each site and each site has a female ward. Each service focuses on patients who suffer with primary diagnosis of mental illness. Many have comorbid substance misuse and some may have comorbid personality disorder, autism spectrum disorder, or mild learning difficulties.

The postholder will provide medical RC responsibility for ward 2 which is an 11 bedded female ward. All patients are detained under the MHA. There is a community case load of about 15 female patients who are care coordinated by the forensic outreach team. Access assessments to the inpatient service and risk advice and management reports are conducted on behalf of the secure provider collaborative on an approximately 1-2 times per monthly basis. Referrals are received from medium security, prisons and acute mental health services within the West Yorkshire Secure Provider Collaborative footprint. Therefore the post holder will be required to travel to other hospitals and prisons.

Leeds Partnerships NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint an 8 PA Consultant Psychiatristin the Leeds Low Secure Female Service based at the Newsam Centre.

Duties will be in line with those of an Approved / Responsible Clinician for low secure patients with complex needs. There will be a requirement for significant liaison with other services and agencies including MAPPA, police, courts, probation etc and support with advice and opinion to general adult colleagues who may seek consultation for patients presenting with particular risks in acute services.

The post holder, supported by the MDT, will provide:

  • Regular routine clinical reviews
  • Flexibility to accommodate urgent clinical reviews
  • Clinical input within the CPA framework
  • To hold Approved Clinician status as defined within the Mental Health Act (1983) and undertake the duties of Responsible Clinician for those subject to the MHA 1983 under their care
  • Complex prescribing and review
  • Effective liaison and collaboration with mental health providers within the trust and the West Yorkshire secure provider collaborative, and with statutory organisations in the effective delivery of safe and effective care and risk management
  • An expectation to work intensively and assertively with the client group
  • To provide professional leadership

The Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (LYPFT) is the main provider of Mental Health and Learning Disability services in Leeds. We also provide specialist inpatient services in York and some highly specialised services across the country. As a teaching trust with strong links to local universities, we are a centre of excellence for teaching, research and development.

There are many benefits of working for LYPFT including fantastic employee wellbeing support, 27 - 33 days annual leave, flexible working and remote working arrangements, the NHS Pension Scheme, coaching, support and opportunities for career development and training and education support alongside a range of exclusive discounts and payment schemes including for cars, extra leave days and more NHS Discount Offers.

We also have a bank department, offering variety of roles in nursing, allied health professions, healthcare support worker and administration clerical. Permanent employees are automatically added to bank.

Applicants should be aware that individuals requiring a visa to work in the UK, the Trust only provides sponsorship for registered healthcare practitioner roles(this does not include Healthcare Support Workers). This is an essential requirement, and the Trust is unable to offer you a role if you do not meet Trust requirements for sponsorship and Home Office requirements for a visa.

employer: East and North Hertfordshire Teaching NHS Trust

descriptionHtml:

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Cardiologist - Cardiac Imaging
descriptionHtml:
Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the largest acute trusts in the North of England with two hospitals serving a local population of 600,000, increasing to 1.2 million for tertiary services. As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

title: Specialist in Gastroenterology

title: Community Dermatology GPwER
descriptionHtml:
The GP with Extended Role (GPwER) in Community Dermatology will deliver high-quality, specialist dermatology care within an NHS England community-based service. The role supports the delivery of care closer to home, reducing unnecessary secondary care referrals and improving patient access in line with NHS Long Term Plan priorities. The post holder will work within agreed clinical pathways, national guidance, and local ICB commissioning arrangements.

We are seeking experienced and committed GPwER Dermatologists to participate in our community service. Undertaking sessional work you will manage your own caseload, as well as autonomous prescribing for patients in our BMJ Award 2021 shortlisted community service.

The role is contract based with a session lasting 3 hours. The number of sessions per week can vary based on clinician availability.

Pay is based on clinical activity.

Clinical Responsibilities

Provide specialist dermatology assessment, diagnosis, and management for patients referred from primary care under locally agreed referral criteria.

Manage a broad range of dermatological conditions, including inflammatory skin disease, benign and suspicious skin lesions, and chronic skin conditions.

Undertake dermatological procedures in line with competencies and service accreditation, which may include cryotherapy, curettage and cautery, punch and shave biopsies, and excision of low-risk skin lesions where approved.

Recognise and appropriately escalate or refer patients requiring secondary or tertiary dermatology services, including suspected skin cancers, in accordance with NHS England cancer pathways and local ICB policies.

Prescribe and monitor dermatological treatments safely and effectively in line with NICE guidance, local formularies, and shared care agreements.

Checking investigation results (commenting and filing)

Documentation & Governance: Maintain accurate and timely clinical records and adhere to governance, safety, and quality standards.

Conduct clinical practice in accordance with contractual requirements and within the parameters of Patient Firsts services plans

Work in face-to-face and telephone clinics as required

Work within changing service requirements as directed by PFSE management/service contract/ specification

Patient FirstSocial Enterprise (PFSE) is a, not for profit, community provider that operates, under NHS ICB contract, across northeast London. Since 2009Patient Firsthas provided a growing number of community services; currently our portfolio consists of: Dermatology, Minor Surgery, Cardiology, MSK and Physiotherapy and Gynaecology. We are a highly reputed service operating for the last 15 years.

The Dermatology service was shortlisted for the prestigious BMJ Dermatology Team of the Year in 2021. Our growing, consultant led, dermatology team consists of experienced GPwERs and specialist nurse prescribers. Operating at locations throughout northeast London (Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest) on weekdays, evenings and Saturday mornings.

We are seeking experienced and committed GPwER Dermatologists to participate in our community service. Undertaking sessional work you will manage your own caseload.

Flexible working opportunities

8 Staff Networks such as, ethnic minority, LGBTQIA+, neurodivergent, women's network, to name a few

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Rheumatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are based on the Diana Princess of Wales Hospital (DPOW) site. We have outpatient clinics at Diana Princess of Wales, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole District Hospital and run these clinics throughout the week over the 3 sites. We see a total outpatient volume of over 13,000 a year across the 3 sites. There are opportunities to further develop MSK ultrasound and connective tissue disease clinics. We work closely with a broad range of services, including General Medicine, Radiology, Orthopaedic Surgery, Paediatrics, Neurology, Academic Chest Medicine, Ophthalmology and Immunology. Regular multidisciplinary meetings facilitate collaborative working and support the delivery of high-quality, effective and safe patient care.

The Rheumatology service provides specialist care to a population of around 450,000, serving communities across North Lincolnshire, North East Lincolnshire, the East Riding of Yorkshire, and Lincolnshire.

We provide inpatient specialist rheumatology care for complex conditions and receive referrals from other specialties across the Trust. There is a weekly rheumatology MDT and we have access to monthly vasculitis MDTs at Hull. This post is designed to support the continued development and delivery of Rheumatology general and specialised services. We would be delighted to support you with any sub-specialty interests. You will have continuing responsibility for patients in your care and to support the functioning of the department. You will be a team player and provide on a reciprocal basis, emergency cover for colleagues during periods of absence. You will carry out teaching duties as required and take an active part in the Undergraduate and Postgraduate Medical Education programme. These include the teaching of junior medical staff as well as the education of nursing staff, general practitioners and other clinical staff. You will have excellent communication skills and be able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ours and your motivation will be to provide high quality care to achieve the best outcomes for patients with common and complex rheumatological conditions.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for enthusiastic and motivated Consultant Anaesthetists to join the Theatres, Anaesthesia and Peri-operative Medicine (TAP) Directorate at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust.

We are seeking skilled, forward-thinking clinicians committed to delivering high-quality patient care within a supportive and innovative multidisciplinary team.

Working across Guy's and St Thomas' Hospitals, successful candidates will gain experience across a diverse range of clinical specialties, including complex elective and emergency surgery, within a leading teaching and research environment.

These roles are particularly suited to anaesthetists who have recently completed specialist training and wish to further develop their clinical expertise, professional interests and leadership skills. Applicants must hold GMC specialist registration and a licence to practise.

Our department offers excellent opportunities for professional development, research, education and innovation. We encourage involvement in peri-operative medicine, quality improvement, teaching, simulation, service development and clinical leadership.

You will join a collaborative and highly respected clinical team, with opportunities to influence practice, contribute to service improvement and help shape the future of anaesthetic care.

We welcome applications from clinicians who share our commitment to excellence, teamwork and continuous improvement

The successful candidates will deliver high-quality anaesthetic care across a range of general and specialist services at Guy's and St Thomas' Hospitals, supporting elective and emergency surgical activity.

Clinical duties will include main theatres, day surgery and specialist services, with opportunities to develop interests in thoracic, vascular and major general surgery, renal transplantation, complex airway management, interventional radiology and peri-operative medicine.

The posts are offered on a full-time 10 Programmed Activity (PA) contract, comprising:

  • 8 PAs - Direct Clinical Care (DCC)

  • 1.5 PAs - Supporting Professional Activities (SPA)

  • 0.5 PA - On-call commitments

The working pattern is predominantly Monday to Friday, with planned weekend activity (approximately one day in ten weeks) and participation in an agreed on-call rota. On-call duties will reflect service requirements and individual expertise across both hospital sites.

Successful candidates will also contribute to teaching, clinical governance, audit, research, quality improvement, service development and clinical leadership.

The Directorate actively supports professional development and the pursuit of individual clinical and academic interests.

A personalised job plan will be agreed within three months of appointment and reviewed annually. Flexible and less-than-full-time working arrangements may be considered, subject to service requirements.

Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's leading NHS organisations, recognised for excellence in patient care, clinical innovation, education and research.

The Theatres, Anaesthesia and Peri-operative Medicine (TAP) Directorate provides comprehensive anaesthetic and peri-operative services across Guy's and St Thomas' Hospitals, supporting a wide range of complex and specialist clinical activity.

Our Anaesthesia Department has an established national and international reputation for clinical excellence, research and innovation, with recognised academic achievements and contributions to leading professional journals and organisations.

Consultants benefit from working within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team across two major teaching hospitals, with opportunities to develop specialist clinical interests and contribute to service improvement.

We are committed to providing a supportive, inclusive and collaborative working environment, offering excellent opportunities in research, education, quality improvement and clinical leadership, alongside continued professional development.

title: Senior Care Assistant
descriptionHtml: As a Senior Care Assistant at HC One, Kindness will be at the core of everything you do. It touches upon every aspect of our Dementia, Nursing, Residential and Specialist care homes. Every single person who works here understands that our residents are people just like them with their own stories to tell. And, by joining us, youll have a wonderful opportunity to give something back to those people.For you, that will mean planning and implementing the kind of care that will give our residents a real sense of security, dignity and independence. You will get to know our residents and their families  helping to ensure we deliver truly personalised care plans. Leading a team of Care Assistants, you will be responsible for maintaining the highest standards of care and youll be a real influence on the rest of the team. Whether you are showing someone how to use a walking frame, helping someone at the end of their life to eat a meal or talking to a residents family on the phone, youll do so with a sense of kindness, above anything else. Assisting the Registered Nurse and Care Manager, you will be involved in providing essential physical and mental stimulation through a range of social and recreational activities, as well as administering medication.At HC-One, our purpose is to support those in our care to lead their best lives. As the Kind Care Company, it is our mission to provide the kindest support and care to Residents living in our care homes, as we strive to be the first-choice care provider for Families, our Colleagues and Commissioners in each of the communities that we serve.

title: Senior Locally Employed Doctor in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Emergency Medicine Team at Wythenshawe Hospital, part of Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust.Previous NHS experience is essential.

We are seeking experienced clinicians to join our senior rota at Junior Registrar levelwho can manage adult and paediatric emergency presentations with a high degree of clinical autonomy. Applicants must have NHS experience and be confident in the assessment and management of critically ill and injured patients. Successful candidates will be expected to undertake middle-grade responsibilities, supervise junior colleagues, and contribute to departmental leadership and patient flow.

We are looking for motivated clinicians with a proven track record of delivering high-quality emergency care within the NHS and who demonstrate the knowledge, skills and professional behaviours expected of a senior Emergency Medicine doctor.

You will be working in one of Greater Manchester's busiest hospitals, where over 100,000 patients are assessed in the Emergency Department each year. Our state-of-the-art department includes a Paediatric Emergency Department, Urgent Treatment Centre, Resuscitation Area and Same Day Emergency Care Unit providing front-door medical and respiratory assessment.

The post offers excellent opportunities to develop specialist interests. Regular simulation sessions, ultrasound training and dedicated consultant-led shop floor teaching are integral parts of the educational programme.

Due to the short-term nature of the role, the successful candidate must hold a current registration with the GMC at the time of application, whether it be an active licence, ceased licence or a pending application -MFT cannot support GMC Sponsorship for vacancies less than 12 months fixed term. Candidates who do not fit this criteria will not progress through to the shortlisting stage.

Please note: MFT is not a right to work sponsoring organisation for Tier 5. Should a candidate require Tier 5 sponsorship, they must apply through the Academy of Royal College via the MTI Scheme.

Please refer to the Job Description and Person Specification for full details. Although this is not a Deanery-approved training post, successful candidates will share the same rota as other trainees.

The post holders will be expected to provide exceptional patient care whilst benefitting from an bespoke training programme and quality improvement activities.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.

At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

employer: Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Dermatology
descriptionHtml:
CONSULTANT IN DERMATOLOGY

We are seeking to recruit enthusiastic, innovative and progressive Consultant Dermatologists to join our Dermatology Team in our large teaching Trust.

The new post holders will join a department of 5 Consultant Dermatologists, 2 Consultant Surgical colleagues, and a dedicated nursing and administration team based at the Birmingham Skin Centre, City Health Campus, SWBH NHS Trust.

The successful candidates will join a well-established self-contained department with an outpatient area, skin theatre and minor procedures area, phototherapy suite, Cutaneous Allergy Unit and a regional Laser unit. Specialist services available in the department include dermatological surgery, tertiary cutaneous allergy, laser therapy, paediatric dermatology, skin cancer, and a biologics service.

The new appointees are expected to have a broad-based dermatology background. The jobs provide general dermatology, paediatric dermatology, skin cancer and other clinics according to sub-specialty areas of interest. Post holders will be supported to develop sub-specialty interest areas in line with service needs.

The successful applicants would also be expected to participate in the in-hours on-call rota for dermatology.

Applicants must be included on the GMC's Specialist Register in Dermatology, or within 6 months of their expected date of receipt of CCT, at the time of interview.

Closing date: Friday 15 December 2026

Interview date: Friday 5 February 2027

Main duties of the job

It is expected that the post holders will have or will develop a subspecialty interest to complement the department and it is anticipated that the successful applicants will also have a well-developed interest in teaching, training and research.

The appointee will take equal responsibility with existing Consultants for the proper functioning of the clinical service, working with clinical and managerial colleagues towards achieving and maintaining national targets.

There will be a commitment to on-call in-hours only as part of this post. There is no out of hours on-call commitment for this post.

A job plan and work schedule will set out agreed arrangements for how work is organised, where it is located, what in general terms the work comprises and when it is to be performed.

The Trust is committed to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching and has strong links to the University of Birmingham and Health Education West Midlands with the Dermatology department having both junior doctors in training, as well as medical students. The department is involved in a variety of research activities with ample opportunities to contribute to these, or initiate relevant dermatology research projects.

Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) serves Birmingham and the Black Country - one of the country's most culturally diverse areas. It's a friendly and welcoming place - a place where you can belong, and a place where you can grow.

We care for our patients, we care about our population, and we care about our people.

Our values - Ambition, Respect and Compassion - are at the heart of who we are. They guide us every step of the way; how we work with each other, and how we look after our patients and their families; how we respect and value the rich diversity of our team and our community.

Our Trust has always aspired to be more than a hospital, more than a healthcare provider. Our purpose is to "Improve the Life Chances and Health Outcomes of our Population." It is what inspires, drives, and unites us every day. It's what makes us unique.

We want working at SWB to feel like more than just a job. We want our Trust to be a place where you can feel you belong. A place where you feel happy, safe, and rewarded. A place where you can develop your career in whatever way you choose. When we say we're 'with you all the way' we want you to know that we mean it. Visit the SWB website to find out more about our ambitions and people plans.

title: Bank Consultant in General and Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
General and Acute Medicine is part of the Acute & Integrated Community Care Directorate at East Cheshire NHS Trust (ECT) which is one of three Directorates within the Trust. The post holder will provide senior expertise within General and Acute Medicine. Be able to manage a full range of presentations in specific area of practice.An autonomous practice framework will be agreed along with this job description, which will outline the defined level of competency for the post holder in relation to independent and autonomous practice.

Applicants must be on the General Medical Council Specialist Register or within six months of being admitted (at the date of interview) to the Register for trainees if in a training programme within the UK. In accordance with the regulations, all other categories of doctors must be on the GMC Specialist Register to be considered for a consultant appointment by the Advisory Appointments Committee.

Applicants must continue to hold a Licence to Practise and full details of the person specification.

Hours per week: Bank

Due to the terms of a Bank contract, we are unable to meet the UKVI Skilled Worked criteria and therefore unable to provide sponsorship for Visa purposes.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

Provide senior clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment and ongoing management for patients within the allocated specialty or service.

Exercise autonomous consultant judgement while working within GMC standards, Trust policies, national guidance and the agreed scope of the assignment.

Provide visible clinical leadership and support safe decision-making, prioritisation, patient flow, escalation and discharge planning.

Lead or participate in consultant ward rounds, post-take ward rounds, board rounds, outpatient clinics, multidisciplinary meetings, handovers and other specialty-specific duties where booked.

Ensure timely senior review of deteriorating or complex patients and obtain or arrange specialist advice, transfer or escalation when required.

We are committed to providing the best quality integrated care to our patients. To achieve this aim we need highly motivated staff who are united by common values and behaviours.

We believe our workforce is our greatest asset and we actively support our staff to develop their capabilities to the full, with a variety of learning and development opportunities.

Whether you are just starting out in your career or are looking to use your skills and experience in a new role, East Cheshire NHS Trust is the right employer for you. We look forward to you joining us so that we can bring out your best.

Please be aware that this post requires an Enhanced DBS (Disclosure and Barring Service) check with barred lists, the cost of which is payable by the successful candidate. If you have lived or worked abroad for 6 months or more in the last 5 years you will need to obtain an overseas police clearance. Further information can be found on the additional information links at the bottom of the advert.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Pears Cumbria School of Medicine Clinical Teaching Fellow
descriptionHtml:
Looking to expand your educational portfolio alongside developing your clinical career? Looking for a special place to explore in your free time? Look no further. Come and join us in our friendly and supportive department on the doorstep of the magnificent Lake District National Park UNESCO world heritage site. It goes almost without saying that with the Lake District on the doorstep there are ample opportunities for a variety of leisure activities.

We're delighted to offer the opportunity to join our experienced team of medical educators in a new venture with Pears Cumbria School of Medicine, a partnership between Imperial College London and the University of Cumbria.

This post will provide the opportunity to develop expertise in undergraduate medical teaching. At the end of the post, it is envisaged you will have a portfolio of competences and experience that will enhance your future career as a clinician and medical educator.

The LTFT post will commence in January 2027 for a fixed term period of 7 months, covering for maternity leave.

The hours of duty will be 20hrs/week with no out-of-hours or weekend working.

This post will require you to work Wednesday - Friday one week and Wednesday and Friday the alternate week. There is no clinical commitment to this post.

The postholder will design, deliver and evaluate teaching sessions for students in the form of small-group tutorials, seminars, simulation and at the bedside, supporting specific clinically focused assessments.

Your time is solely in Medical Education and will be directed towards planning and delivering the General Surgery, including breast surgery, year 2 PCSM curriculum.

We will encourage you to attend educational training sessions both locally and in the North East, where appropriate, and as your confidence grows, to help mentor other clinical colleagues as educators.

The experienced undergraduate tutors and Programme Director will provide support and mentorship with your development as a teacher.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

  • Being a clinically led organisation
  • Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust
  • A positive patient experience every time
  • A great place to work
  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

employer: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Speciality Doctor in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Specialty Doctor to join an innovative team within Emergency Medicine dedicated to the delivery of high quality care within Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. This post is to cover Maternity Leave.

Whilst on duty a doctor has clinical and professional responsibility for their patients. It is also the duty of a doctor to:

Keep patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) informed about their condition.

Involve patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) in decision-making about their treatment.

Maintain professional standards and obligations as set out from time to time by the General Medical Council (GMC) and comply with GMC's guidance on 'Good Medical Practice' as amended or substituted from time to time.

A doctor is responsible for carrying out any work related to and reasonably incidental to the duties set out in the Job Plan such as:

The keeping of records and the provision of reports.

The proper delegation of tasks.

Maintaining skills and knowledge.

Doctors will be expected to be flexible and to cooperate with reasonable requests to cover for their colleagues' absence where they are safe and competent and where it is practicable to do so.

The overriding purpose is to support the provision of the highest quality patient care through personal actions and continuous improvement.

- This post is based at King's Mill Hospital but may also undertake programmed activities at Newark Hospital if required.

- Under the supervision of the Consultant in Emergency Medicine, provide to the care of patients in the department with responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of illness or injury.

- Referral of patients to appropriate inpatient facilities as appropriate.

- Outpatient programmed activities depending on the needs of patients.

- Teaching and supervision of junior medical staff and nursing staff as appropriate.

- Active involvement in audit, clinical governance, and the development of departmental policies.

- So far as is consistent with the discharge of the above duties, the post-holder shall undertake to deputise for absent colleagues, when the post-holder deputises outside his/her normal contracted duties and commitment, an equivalent amount of off-duty shall be given.

- The post-holder undertakes to be available for such irregular commitments outside normal reserved duties as are essential for the continuity of patient care.

- To take responsibility for your own continuing professional education in accordance with guidelines set out by the appropriate college/faculty/professional body.

We are an award-winning NHS Foundation Trust working alongside health and social care colleagues across the county to provide acute and community healthcare services to more than 420,000 people across Mansfield, Ashfield, Newark and Sherwood, and parts of Derbyshire and Lincolnshire.

We put the patient at the heart of everything that we do and it is our aim to make sure that every patient is treated as we would want a member of our own family to be treated. At the same time, we expect our staff to be caring, kind and courteous to each other and to look out for each other. We believe that we are truly a clinically-led organisation.

We are proud that our Trust colleagues have voted us the best acute Trust to work for in the East Midlands for seven years running in the National NHS Staff Survey, while the Care Quality Commission has rated our Trust as 'outstanding' for care and our King's Mill Hospital as the only 'outstanding' NHS-run hospital in the East Midlands.

employer: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Director Genomic Medicine Service - Rare Disease
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious individual to join our well integrated team.

The NEY GMS brings together regional Clinical and Laboratory Partners, all working together to improve health and equity of access to genomic tests, diagnosis and related treatments for patients in the region.

The NEY GMS is led by four partner trusts: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, The Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. There are around 500 medical, scientific, technologist, counselling and support staff focused entirely on Genomics. They support a much larger network of mainstream clinicians including Oncologists, Pathologists, Neurologists, Obstetricians, Paediatricians, Nurses and Pharmacists who use genomic diagnosis to support clinical decision making and improve patient care.

The NEY GMS is governed via a partnership arrangement that is delivered by a regional GMS executive team which has operational responsibility for the quality of services. The GMS executive team is accountable to the NEY GMS Partnership Board which includes representation from partner Trusts.

Closing date: 11 November 2026 @ midnight

Interview Date: TBC

The Clinical Director - Rare Disease, working as part of the NEY GMS Executive Team, will lead the strategic development of the Rare Disease clinical function across the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Medicine Service. The role will provide senior clinical leadership to support equitable access to genomic testing, diagnosis and personalised care pathways for patients with rare and inherited conditions. The role will bring together clinicians, clinical genetics services and laboratory partners across the region to drive innovation, improve patient outcomes and ensure the effective implementation of genomic medicine at scale.

We are aiming to appoint a highly credible and influential clinical leader with a proven track record of leading service transformation, and the strategic insight to drive innovation across complex healthcare systems. The role will combine clinical and scientific credibility with strong executive leadership, demonstrating the ability to shape regional and national agendas, build effective partnerships across organisational boundaries, and deliver measurable improvements in quality, access, and patient outcomes.

For an informal discussion and further information regarding the opportunity and Directorate, please contact: Mr Neville Gaukroger (NEY GMS Managing Director)via email Neville.Gaukroger@nhs.net

Please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification document for full details of the role and essential criteria.

As a flexible working friendly organisation, we want to be sure that you can work in a way that is best for us and for our patients, and for you. Speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate a flexible working arrangement. If it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you.

With around 2 million contacts with patients every year, we deliver care from:

  • Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI)
  • Freeman Hospital
  • Newcastle Dental Hospital
  • Cramlington Manor Walks
  • Urgent treatment centres
  • Newcastle Fertility Centre
  • Northern Centre for Cancer Care, North Cumbria
  • Northern Genetics Service

These include a range of flagship services which deliver cutting-edge care (supported by state-of-the-art diagnostic services in both radiology and pathology) and are a catalyst for innovation to support pioneering clinical practice in the NHS.

We also have offices at Regent Point in Gosforth and community sites.

Please see attached information on what Staff Benefits we have to offer at our Trust under 'Documents to download' or 'Supporting documents'.

For further information on Careers at The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust please visit our website: Newcastle Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
Horden Group Practice are currently looking for an enthusiastic salaried GP to join our friendly and well-respected practice team. We are a 3 partner training practice based across 2 sites (that are within close proximity of each other) in Horden/Peterlee, County Durham. The role is for 6 sessions per week (Wednesday-Friday). The successful applicant will aslo be required to work our Monday evening surgery on a pro-rata basis.

Our last CQC rating was good.

The delivery of highly effective medical care to the entitled population

The provision of services commensurate with the GMS contract

Generic prescribing adhering to local and national guidance

Effective management of long-term conditions

Processing of administration in a timely manner, including referrals, repeat prescription requests and other associated administrative tasks

On a rotational basis, undertake telephone triage and duty doctor roles

Maintain accurate clinical records in conjunction with good practice, policy and guidance

Working collaboratively, accepting an equal share of the practice workload

Adhere to best practice recommended through clinical guidelines and the audit process

Contribute to the successful implementation of continuous improvement and quality initiatives within the practice

Accept delegated responsibility for a specific area (or areas) or the QOF

Attend and contribute effectively to practice meetings as required

Contribute effective to the development and maintenance of the practice including; clinical governance, training

Commit to self-learning and instil an ethos of continuing professional development across the practice team

Support the partners in achieving the strategic aims of the practice, making recommendations to enhance income and reduce expenditure

Review and adhere to practice protocols and policies at all times

Helping to provide supervision to our GP Registrar trainees.

Horden Group Practice are a 3-partner training practice with 2 sites. Our main site is in Horden and our branch site is in Peterlee. Our team is made up of GPs, GP Registrars, ANP's, Practice Nurses, Pharmacists and HCA's who are all supported by our experienced helpful Admin Team. We also have ARRS roles linked to the Surgery.

The applicant should have excellent communication and interpersonal skills and be able to provide high quality, patient-centred care. Dependant on experience we will offer a competitive salary and NHS pension.

employer: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Neurosurgery
descriptionHtml:
Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a Junior Clinical Fellow in Neurosurgery to join our team. The appointment will commence on 03 February 2027 and will be a permanent contract.

Applicants should have a medical degree or primary medical qualification from a recognised university or institution and registered with the General Medical Council with a license to practise. They are also required to have evidence of foundation competencies with a minimum of 12 months clinical experience post eligibility for full registration with the GMC

These post does not award a National Training Number. As this post is not recognised as a 'training post', full registration with the GMC with a licence to practise is required, and if the appointee does not hold right of residence in the UK sponsorship will be required. The duties of these posts are equivalent to an ST1-2 trainee in Neurosurgery

The interview process will be held in 2 stages on Thursday 26th November 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to take part in a Clinical Station followed by a formal Interview.

Candidates deemed suitable for interview may also be considered for any further vacancies that arise during the recruitment process.

The Sheffield Neurosurgical Department is a regional unit serving a population of approximately 2.2 million covering South Yorkshire, North Derbyshire, and North Lincolnshire. The Adult Neurosurgical Service is based at the Royal Hallamshire Hospital with a 52 bed unit, including a 7 bed Neuro-Critical care and a 13 bed HDU. The Paediatric Neurosurgical Service is separately located at Sheffield Children's Hospital immediately adjacent to the Royal Hallamshire Hospital. The Sheffield Neurosurgical Unit also includes the National Centre for Stereotactic Radiosurgery which comprises two gamma knives, including a Lexsell Perfexion

Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's busiest and most successful NHS foundation trusts. We provide a full range of local hospital and community services for people in Sheffield, as well as specialist care for patients from further afield, including cancer, spinal cord injuries, renal and cardiothoracic services. In addition to community health services, the Trust comprises five of Yorkshire's best known teaching hospitals.

The Royal Hallamshire Hospital

The Northern General Hospital

Charles Clifford Dental Hospital

Weston Park Cancer Hospital

Jessop Wing Maternity Hospital

The Trust has a history of high quality care, clinical excellence and innovation in medical research. We strive to promote a culture of continuous quality improvement and encourage our staff to innovate and adopt 'best practice' in order to deliver the highest standard of care to our patients.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Otolaryngology with Interest in Head & Neck
descriptionHtml:
Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust is looking to appoint a Head and Neck Surgical Oncology Fellow. This is a fixed term post for a duration of 12 months. The post holder should be post CCT. They must have experience of working within the NHS and be able to demonstrate a good command of the English language. Candidates are encouraged to visit the Department after short listing and should contact Mrs Lisa Fraser or Mr Rajeev Mathew on 01865226929.

This is an exciting opportunity to work in a high-volume prestigious head and neck centre, providing both secondary and tertiary level care. As a tertiary referral centre, the department manages major complex head and neck cases across Berkshire, Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon and Milton Keynes. This includes both malignant and complex benign work.

This is a 12-month fellowship, aimed at candidates approaching the end of their higher surgical training with the FRCS ORL-HNS or equivalent, or post-CCT. We welcome International candidates, who should make contact directly with the Fellowship organisers to discuss eligibility prior to application.

The successful candidate will have a central role in the management of head and neck patients both in clinic, on the ward, decision making in the MDT and operating. There are opportunities to become involved in research as well as NIHR studies.

Our goal is to extend the candidate's surgical competency to that of a safe independent practitioner working within a head and neck multi-disciplinary team. On completion of the programme it is intended that the Fellow will be fully prepared to assume a Consultant position in a tertiary head and neck unit.

Surgical responsibility during the year will be tailored on a personalised basis depending on the candidate's progress, with progressively increasing responsibility in major cases. Teaching of registrars will be an important component of the Fellowship, in preparation for assuming a future Consultant position.

The successful candidate will have an initial meeting with their educational supervisor, and a discussion regarding objectives. Regular informal trainer feedback and periodic, formal evaluation of progress will occur within the fellowship. It is expected the candidate maintains an operative log during the fellowship, as well as further evidence when available e.g. patient feedback, reflective practice.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest and most respected NHS teaching trusts, providing world-class healthcare across four hospitals: the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre and Horton General Hospital and over one hundred satellite sites. Find out more information here OUH at a Glance 2026/27

You'll become part of an organisation at the forefront of patient care, research, education and innovation. You'll have access to excellent learning and development opportunities, work alongside highly skilled multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to services that make a real difference.

Our commitment toDelivering Compassionate Excellence is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence, we strive to create an environment where staff feel supported, valued and empowered to thrive. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel and the OneTeamOneOUH - LIVING OUR VALUES video.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, respectful and safe workplace for everyone. As signatories to the NHS Sexual Safety Charter, we have a zero-tolerance approach to inappropriate behaviour and are dedicated to fostering a culture where all colleagues feel welcomed, respected and able to be themselves. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to theten core principles.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Swarland Avenue Surgery is looking to appoint a motivated, caring and enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive practice for 5-6 sessions per week. The successful candidate will provide high-quality, patient-centred care, manage a varied clinical workload and work collaboratively with our multidisciplinary team to meet the needs of our patient population.

Why Join Us?

Thanks to our supportive team and culture, the practice provides a small, friendly and traditional working environment.

We value teamworking and the GP team meet daily for clinical discussions.

We recognise how important it is to find the right practice. If you would like to know more about us, the practice and the post, we would welcome informal discussions and visits. Please contact Beth Foster, Practice Manager at bethfoster@nhs.net

title: GP Vacancy  The Medical Centre, Southall (UB1 1JH)
descriptionHtml:
Join our friendly, forward-thinking team at The Medical Centre, Southall, where you can make a real difference through personalised care for patients with acute and long-term conditions. We are seeking an enthusiastic GP with experience in diabetes management for eight sessions per week, with salaried or long-term locum options and job sharing considered.

With engaged clinical leadership, strong links to our local Primary Care Network and plans to become a GP training practice in February 2027, this is an exciting time to join us and help shape our practices future. The role is primarily based in Southall, with occasional cover at our W12 sit

Location: Primarily on-site in Southall, with occasional cover/working required at our W12 7FG site.Sessions: 8 per week (Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays). title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Community Eating Disorders
descriptionHtml:
East London NHS Foundation Trust runs a specialist Community Eating Disorders Service (CEDS) providing specialist assessment and treatment to people referred with severe and complex eating disorders. We have a stepped care partnership with local charity 'Caroline' who are commissioned to provide for mild to moderate eating disorders.

The team works in close conjunction with primary care and secondary mental health services and manages approximately 200-300 referrals per year with an ongoing caseload of circa 70, with average of 30 at high risk. The EDS consists of a multi-disciplinary community team comprising psychology, psychiatry, mental and physical health nursing, GP with special interest, Occupational Therapists and dietetics colleagues.

The current team delivers evidence-based treatments within a recovery model of care. We work using a motivational approach with patients to empower them in taking ownership of their recovery. To promote recovery positive risk taking and effective risk management are essential.

Interview date (AAC panel):TBC

Provide consultant leadership and support the continued development of the Eating Disorder services.

Ensure that service users consistently receive high-quality services that adhere to the best practice guidelines and achieve high professional standards.

Provide a key role as the senior specialist clinician within the team and support the wider work of the multi-disciplinary team.

Provide a comprehensive assessment of complex referrals requiring psychiatric review. This includes medical and psychiatric assessment, including eating disorder and non-eating disorder psychopathology.

Provide consultations as part of the MEED pathway with colleagues from acute hospitals.

Lead in the monitoring and treatment of the physical complications of eating disorders in collaboration with other health professionals.

Supervise the team in charge of the medical monitoring and management of High-risk patients monitored in House (checking bloods when needed, taking appropriate actions).

Provide clinical advice and guidance to primary care physicians to manage patients in the least restrictive environment.

Work with the Team manager to ensure KPI and national targets are met.

Our mission is to make a positive difference to people's lives by improving the quality of life for all we serve. Our values are: We Care, We Respect, We are Inclusive - so we are looking for people who live and breathe these qualities when supporting service users and carers, and in their relationships with colleagues in the Trust and our partner organisations.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Job Title:Consultant Psychiatrist

Service Line: Male Low Secure Mental Health

Professionally Accountable to:Medical Director

Managerially Responsible to:Hospital Manager

We are seeking an experienced full-time (10 programmed activities) Consultant Psychiatrist who will work at Cygnet Hospital Bury Hudson and provide senior medical cover on Low Secure Service across Upper East and East Hampton LSU wards. The caseload will be Upper East (13 inpatients) and half of East Hampton (7 inpatients)

Upper East and East Hampton are our low secure services for men with mental illness, and both support men experiencing complex mental illness and/or personality disorder.

The services accept direct admissions from the community, from rehabilitation or acute services and from prison, however many people step down through the internal care pathway from the medium secure services offered at Cygnet Bury Hudson.

Across all of our medium and low secure services, service users are supported by a dedicated multi-disciplinary team who work with people to assess their needs and create a discharge pathway to the community. The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician and will oversee and maintain the care of all ward inpatients as required and will also have responsibility for auditing the medical services rendered at the ward and ensuring their good quality in accordance to GMC standards of good medical practice and other relevant professional guidelines.

In this role, your expertise will be the driving force for life-changing treatment fully supported by a Specialty Doctor and first-class multidisciplinary team including qualified nurses, psychologist and occupational therapist.

And youll have the opportunity to progress to Medical Director Level through our management schemes.

At Cygnet, youll enjoy excellent professional development, shopping, travel and leisure discounts as well as a range of healthcare and financial benefits to support you to be happy both in and out of work.

Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others every day.

employer: Honeybeerecruitment.com Ltd. trading as Military Medical Personnel (MMP)

title: Healthcare Assistant

We offer -
